title: P@x schedule
description: One reminder or scheduled task (AI control layer, sections 5.6 and 16.2), with the standing approvals it owns, as stored in <store>/schedules/definitions/<id>.json. A schedule exists only because the user created it from a proposal; the assistant can propose one and cannot write this file. The loader in services/tur-pax-memory is authoritative. It also enforces what this schema cannot express: sizes are counted in bytes, not characters; text fields hold no control characters (a message or request may hold line breaks and tabs); the zone is a name in the IANA time-zone database; an interval is at least 300 seconds and at most 3660 days; a weekly trigger names no weekday twice; the arguments of a standing approval are at most 16384 bytes as JSON; confirmed_at is not before created_at; and the identifier equals the file name.

timestamp.description: Whole seconds since the Unix epoch, UTC. At most the last second of the year 9999.

local_time.description: A wall-clock time of day, HH:MM, from 00:00 to 23:59.

zone.description: The IANA time zone a wall-clock time is in, for example Europe/Rome.

standing_approval.description: An approval the user gave when creating the schedule, for one exact tool call. A call matches only if the service, the tool and every argument are identical; numbers compare as written, so 1 and 1.0 differ. The same three properties as the policy engine's StandingApproval.

service.description: The D-Bus name of the service that owns the tool.

arguments.description: The complete arguments of the approved call.

reminder.description: Notify the user. A reminder performs no action and cannot carry a standing approval.

task.description: Run a request, unattended. A class 2 action runs only if it matches one of the standing approvals; otherwise it is deferred and offered to the user on return.

trigger_every.description: At anchor + k * interval for k = 0, 1, 2, ... The interval is elapsed time: a day is 86400 seconds.

trigger_daily.description: Every day at a wall-clock time. A time that does not exist on a day (clocks go forward) fires when the gap ends; a time that occurs twice (clocks go back) fires the first time only.

trigger_weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a wall-clock time.

trigger_monthly.description: On a day of the month at a wall-clock time. In a month that lacks the day: last_day (the default) fires on the month's last day, skip does not fire that month.

trigger_event.description: When a named system event happens. It does not fire again within 300 seconds of its last run.

id.description: The schedule identifier: s- and 8 to 16 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

name.description: A short name, shown in settings and, reduced to safe characters, in the timer's description.

missed_runs.description: What happens to occurrences that passed while the machine was off. run_once: one run on return, however many were missed. skip: none; wait for the next occurrence.

created_at.description: When the user first created the schedule.

confirmed_at.description: When the user created or last changed the schedule. Occurrences are counted from here.

proposed_by_task.description: The task during which the assistant proposed the schedule.
